From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: November KPI heatmap & action rotations — prep for exec QBR

Team — attaching the November KPI heatmap plus the cost-driver breakdown. High level notes: latency has a concentrated regression on the long-tail (p95-p99) driven by two recent model rollouts; unit-cost increased ~12% MoM due to a combination of larger sequence lengths and higher burst capacity usage; uptime is nominal but we had two short infra events captured in the incident log.

Requests:
- Vivek: quick triage on the p99 tail — please call out if this is model kernel or infra scheduling.
- Laura: can you put together a single-slide executive summary highlighting the business impact (QBR ask).
- Irene: confirm whether we can push a lightweight quantized fallback for the flagged model variants for the canary group.

Goal: have slide deck + 1-page heatmap notes by EOD Monday so we can sync with CS (Nimbus) Tuesday morning.

Attachments: 2026-11-latency-heatmap.pdf, monthly-cost-driver-breakdown.xlsx, uptime-incident-log-Nov2026.txt

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Field Ops (acting)
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-28T14:56:00-08:00
Subject: Re: November KPI heatmap & action rotations — prep for exec QBR

On Sat, Nov 28, 2026 at 11:03 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> I can have a first pass by Monday 10:30 PT.

Quick triage notes — high level:
- Root cause: scheduling fragmentation combined with one kernel path regression on the new attention block for model variant m-xl-2q. Profiling shows increased context-switch waits for longer sequences (>1.5k tokens).
- Mitigations (short): revert the kernel change for canary, adjust batch sampler to prefer shorter seqs during peak, enable prefix KV caching aggressively for suspect tenants.
- Mitigations (medium): ship a quantized fallback (m-xl-2q-q8) behind routing policy for tiered customers.

I'll prep a 1-page triage doc (profiling snippets + recommended rollback/flags) and share by Monday 9:00 PT. If Irene can validate fallback feasibility, we can include an ETA on rollout.

Vivek
Sr Director, Serving Runtime

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: November KPI heatmap & action rotations — prep for exec QBR

On Sun, Nov 28, 2026 at 02:56 PM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick triage notes — high level: Root cause: scheduling fragmentation + kernel regression on m-xl-2q.

Checked compatibility for the quantized fallback: good news — m-xl-2q-q8 is stable on the current runtime and we've got prebuilt kernels for the main HW families. Effort estimate: 1 engineer * 2.5 days to wire up routing + smoke tests for canary; 1 day to create rollback toggle.

I'll block engineering cycles Tuesday-Thursday. Also flagged possible perf delta: expect ~6-9% quality drift in long-context generation; we'll need product/CS for customer communication.

Irene
Principal Engineer, Runtime

From: Sofia Rami <sofia.rami@acme-ml.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Thanks for the heads up — ACME saw a spike in tail latency on Nov 24–26 which matched increased long-document summarize jobs. We appreciate the proposed mitigations; CS asked whether the quantized fallback will be opt-in per-tenant or applied only behind a routing rule for Canary. Also can we get a brief note to send to customers explaining the temporary quality delta and the rollback plan?

Attachments requested: ACME request for latency sample logs (we'll upload to your shared drive).

— Sofia Rami
Head of Platform Engineering, ACME-ML
